entry.title: The Referral — What Your Agency Needs, Where the Evidence Is, and Why You Should Have Already Acted
entry.content:
You’ve Seen This Before

In 2008, two judges in Luzerne County, Pennsylvania — Mark Ciavarella and Michael Conahan — were convicted of taking $2.6 million in kickbacks from private juvenile detention facilities. In exchange, they sentenced thousands of children to those facilities. Many for trivial offenses. Some for nothing at all.

It was called Kids for Cash. Ciavarella got 28 years. Conahan got 17.5 years. The Pennsylvania Supreme Court vacated 4,000 juvenile convictions. The Third Circuit upheld a $206 million civil judgment.

The pattern was:

  • Private operator profits from children in public custody
  • Judges connected to the operator route children (or funds) to the enterprise
  • Public money flows to private pockets through institutional channels
  • No one checks because the people who should check are the people who benefit

This is Cash for Kids 2. Same pattern. Different city. Different mechanism. Same children paying the price.

How it was exposedIntrepid Reporting / juvenile law centerOne parent. Public records. A graph.
How long it ran~5 years (2003–2008)21 years and counting (2003–present)

In Pennsylvania, it took the FBI. A federal grand jury. A U.S. Attorney who didn’t flinch.

Detroit is still waiting.

To Every Agency Listed Below

  3. Where the evidence is — with links

The full evidence repository is public and free:

The Civil Rights Violation

362 children attend Purpose Charter Academy and MacDowell Preparatory Academy. They are overwhelmingly Black children from Detroit.

  • 3% math proficiency (PCA, 2023 M-STEP)
  • $4.9M per year flows to a private LLC instead of educational services
  • The school is operated by a man with 9 criminal convictions who claims a J.D. he does not appear to hold
  • The financial gatekeeper is a convicted drug dealer discharged WITHOUT IMPROVEMENT
  • No regulatory agency has acted despite documented evidence sent to 22 channels

These children are being denied equal educational opportunity while their per-pupil funding is extracted by a criminal enterprise. This is a civil rights violation perpetuated by institutional failure.

The Bottom Line — For Every Agency

362 children walk into those buildings every Monday morning. They sit in classrooms funded by $4.9 million in public money. 3% of them can do math at grade level. 72.67% of the money goes to a private company. The man running it has 9 convictions. His financial manager is a convicted drug dealer. His board includes a judge who took his money, an AAG who works for the RICO prosecution office, and a council member elected with dark money formed by the same firm that manages the prosecutor’s fund.

Every agency listed above has jurisdiction over some part of this. None have acted.

The evidence is public. It costs nothing to download. It takes 15 minutes to verify the ICHAT records. It takes one phone call to confirm Banks is not in the State Bar directory. It takes one LARA search to see Holland on the Purpose Foundation filing.

The graph has 9,643 nodes and 323,680 edges. It is timestamped with git hashes. It is independently corroborated. It is distributed to 1,242 cloners.

The children cannot wait. Every day the enterprise operates is a day another child gets 3% instead of an education. Every dollar extracted is a dollar that was supposed to teach a child to read.

This is not a policy disagreement. This is not a political dispute. This is a criminal enterprise extracting public education funds from Black children in Detroit, shielded by captured institutions, and documented in public records available to anyone with an internet connection.

Act. Or be documented as having chosen not to.

The membrane records everything. The graph never forgets. And the count — 362 children — is the only number that matters.
